### LA-IMM-04 — SC `sc_pti_17_22_150`

- **PATHWAYS:** `SC:diversion-or-program-completion-expungement`
- **PACKET FAMILIES:** rcap-sc-custom-pleading
- **QUESTION:** The single-incident fee. Section 17-22-940(G) as amended by 2018 Act No. 254 was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides that where multiple charges from a single incident are combined under § 17-1-40 or § 17-22-150(a), 'only one two hundred fifty-dollar fee, one twenty-five dollar SLED verification fee, and one thirty-five dollar clerk of court filing fee may be charged'. The controlling review reports the single-incident solicitor fee as one hundred fifty dollars, drawn from Supreme Court expungement guidance. The current statutory figure is two hundred fifty dollars. The packet quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one.
- **CONTROLLING AUTHORITIES:** S.C. Code § 17-22-150(a); S.C. Code § 17-22-110; S.C. Code § 17-22-930; S.C. Code § 17-22-940(D); S.C. Code § 17-22-940(E); S.C. Code § 17-22-940(G); S.C. Code § 17-1-40

- **EXISTING PRODUCT TREATMENT:** Family bridged; packet generation and payment closed pending this answer.
- **CONFLICT OR MISSING ELEMENT:** Two authorities give different single-incident fees. S.C. - **OPTIONS:** (1) Quote the statutory $250 figure. (2) Quote the Supreme Court guidance figure of $150. (3) Quote both with an explanation of which applies when.
- **RECOMMENDED INTERIM TREATMENT:** The packet already quotes the statutory figure and does not promise the lower one. Keep that until counsel decides.
- **EXACT DECISION REQUESTED:** Does the $150 single-incident fee in the Supreme Court expungement guidance survive the 2018 amendment to S.C. Code § 17-22-940(G), and which figure does the packet quote?

- **ENGINEERING CHANGE AFTER ANSWER:** Set the fee figure in the SC custom pleading and re-render the family.

| Q-009 | ME | `me-nonconv` | legal_effect_or_warning | LEGAL_DECISION_RESOLVED_GUIDANCE | Whether a charge dismissed after successful completion of a deferred disposition under 17-A M.R.S. ch. 67 subch. 4 is confidential criminal history record information under 16 M.R.S. § 703(2). This was checked against current official text and is NOT ESTABLISHED. Section 703(2) lists paragraphs A through L and none mentions a deferred disposition. The closest is paragraph G, which reaches a charge 'dismissed with prejudice by the court or dismissed with finality by a prosecutor outside a plea agreement'. Under 17-A M.R.S. § 1903 the State dismisses the charging instrument WITH PREJUDICE on compliance, which fits the first clause, but a deferred disposition arises from a written agreement between the defendant and the State, which arguably falls inside paragraph G's outside-a-plea-agreement carve-out. Section 1903 says nothing about confidentiality or sealing. No statute, State Bureau of Identification guidance, Judicial Branch page or Law Court decision resolves it. The packet therefore fails closed: it does not promise confidentiality on the strength of the deferred-disposition label, it tells the participant to verify what the Bureau record actually shows, and it routes the correction request only where the record is demonstrably inaccurate. |
| Q-010 | ME | `me-seal-gen` | notice_or_service | SOURCE_ACQUISITION_REQUIRED | Whether the movant must serve the prosecutorial office, or whether the court performs all notice. 15 M.R.S. § 2264(3) directs notice to the prosecutorial office that represented the State but does not assign the act to the movant, and none of CR-218, CR-289 or CR-307 carries a certificate-of-service block — unlike the juvenile form JV-043, which states on its face that the petitioner must provide a copy to the prosecuting attorney. The packet fails closed: it tells the participant that the court is understood to give notice, and that they should confirm with the clerk at filing and deliver a courtesy copy if the clerk asks. |
| Q-011 | ME | `me-seal-survivor` | legal_effect_or_warning | SOURCE_ACQUISITION_REQUIRED | Form CR-308 page 2 carries a warning box stating that if at any time after the date of the order the defendant is convicted of a new crime in Maine or in any other jurisdiction, the new conviction extinguishes the order. That is inconsistent with 15 M.R.S. § 2264(7) as amended by PL 2025, c. 513, which now provides in terms that the subsection does not apply to records sealed pursuant to section 2262-A or 2262-B. | Q-048 | WV | `wv_common_conv_procedure` | venue | ATTORNEY_OR_PARTNER_HANDOFF | Venue on a multi-county conviction petition. The controlling review states that S.B. 562 (2020) allows a person seeking expungement of convictions in more than one county to file in his or her county of residence. Section 61-11-26 was read in full at source on 2026-08-06 and the current text does not contain a residence-county venue option: subsections (a)(1) and (a)(2) both say 'petition the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred', the subsection (d) proviso requires a multiple-misdemeanour petition to 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable', and § 61-11-26a(a) says 'may petition the circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred'. Read together the current text supports one petition covering several counties, grouped by circuit court and served on the prosecuting attorney of each county of conviction, but it does not name a residence-county forum. Venue for the single-county case is unaffected and unambiguous. Until counsel resolves this, the packet directs a multi-county participant to the circuit court of conviction and adds a local-check instruction rather than promising a residence-county filing. |
| Q-049 | WV | `wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors` | venue | ATTORNEY_OR_PARTNER_HANDOFF | Where a multiple-misdemeanour group spans more than one county, which circuit court receives the single petition. Section 61-11-26 was read in full at source on 2026-08-06: subsection (a)(1) says 'the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred', and the subsection (d) proviso requires the petition to 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable'. Together those support one petition covering several counties, but the text does not say which of the several circuit courts is the forum, and it does not contain the county-of-residence option the controlling review attributes to S.B. 562. Until counsel answers, the packet directs the participant to the circuit court of conviction and, for a genuinely multi-county group, to a lawyer. |

| Q-052 | WV | `wv_conv_single_misdemeanor` | correct_form | ARTIFACT_LEGAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED | Which published form is the operative § 61-11-26 misdemeanour petition. The Judiciary Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms. SCA-C900, captioned 'Instructions for Expungement of Records Petition' and revised 04/01/2021, is a five-page document whose pages 2 to 5 are themselves a petition, verification and certificate of service. That embedded petition is materially stale: it requires the petitioner to have been 'between eighteen and twenty-six years of age', requires 'no prior or subsequent convictions other than minor traffic violations', recites 'W. Va. Code §61-11-26 (2009)', and cross-references the exclusion list to '§61-11-26(i)', all of which are features of the pre-2019 section. The section in force places exclusions at subsection (c) and imposes no age limit. SCA-C906 matches the current subsection (c) and (d) structure and carries the § 61-11-26a elections, and is therefore used here. The packet must not generate the SCA-C900 embedded petition. Whether the Judiciary intends SCA-C900 to remain published in that form is not established. |

The form's operative paragraphs still track the current subsection (a) requirements for a straight acquittal or dismissal, so the fit is sound for this track, but whether the Judiciary intends the 2000 recital to be corrected, and whether any circuit rejects the form on that basis, is not established. |
| Q-055 | WV | `wv_nc_diversion_deferred` | correct_form | ARTIFACT_LEGAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED | Whether SCA-C903 is the right vehicle for a deferred-adjudication dismissal. The form was read at source on 2026-08-06: it is captioned 'for Reasons Other than Entry of a Plea', recites 'W.Va. Code § 61-11-25 (2000)', carries a single charge block with one free-text reason-for-dismissal field, has no same-transaction-or-occurrence paragraph and no diversion or deferred-adjudication paragraph, and requires the movant to state that the dismissal 'was not in exchange for a guilty plea to another offense'. Section 61-11-22a operates on an entered guilty plea which is withdrawn on compliance, so the movant's statement is literally true — the dismissal is not in exchange for a plea to another offence — but the caption and the missing paragraphs make the fit imperfect. The packet therefore generates the official form plus a supplemental pleading carrying the statutory basis, the same-transaction recital and the carve-out recital. Whether the Judiciary regards SCA-C903 as the correct form for this route, or whether a distinct form or a full custom petition is expected, is not established. |
| Q-056 | WV | `wv_pardon_expungement` | legal_effect_or_warning | LEGAL_DECISION_RESOLVED_GUIDANCE | Whether § 5-1-16a(b) is the whole of the effect of a pardon expungement. The subsection was read at source on 2026-08-06 and provides only that the expunged record may not be considered in an application to a West Virginia educational institution or in an application for a licence required by a West Virginia professional organisation. Unlike §§ 61-11-25(e) and 61-11-26(l), it contains no general non-disclosure provision and no statement that the proceedings are considered never to have occurred. What the packet may tell a participant about disclosing the record to an ordinary employer after a § 5-1-16a expungement is therefore not settled. |
